explanation: The Fourth Coalition article makes the Third Coalition the reason for the Fourth: "Excluding Prussia, some members of the coalition had previously been fighting France as part of the Third Coalition, and there was no intervening period of general peace. On 9 October 1806, Prussia declared war on France and joined a renewed coalition, fearing the rise in French power after the defeat of Austria and establishment of the French-sponsored Confederation of the Rhine in addition to having learned of French plans to cede Prussian-desired Hanover to Britain in exchange for peace." `caused`: the article names the Third Coalition's own outcome — Austria defeated, the Confederation of the Rhine set up — as what brought Prussia in, and says there was no peace in between. Probable, and on the article alone at one revision: the lead carries no footnote of its own, so there is no locator for a second author.
